descriptor.scene: High morning sky. The elevator car climbs its silver ribbon exactly as the locked ascending plate paints it: the cylindrical brass-and-glass car warm with inner light, the ribbon running dead vertical through the whole frame, the jungle canopy far below reading as a soft green sea. The car rides in the lower left third of the frame. Inside the glass, three small founder figures stand together, tiny and warm, no faces readable. Up in the upper right, still distant but nearer than it has ever been, floats the island exactly as its locked establishing plate paints it: teardrop rock, terraced gardens, brass spires, catching the sunrise like a promise being kept. The ribbon points at it. Keep the lower right calm: open canopy and morning haze.
descriptor._caption: The doors are open and the light inside is warm, and there are seats enough for three. The jungle lets go of them trail by trail, and the island comes up like a sunrise.

Any figures sit inside the space at full length and no taller than half the frame, so the room, its geometry and its light all read at once. the-camouflaged-elevator exactly as its reference plate: A space elevator hidden in the jungle: one rounded brass-and-glass car standing on a low round stone platform, a brass collar above the car, and a slender silver ribbon rising dead vertical from the collar out of every frame toward the island. There are many such elevators in the jungle and every one is this same design. The car is 2.6 m tall by 2.0 m wide with a 0.9 m sliding double door on the front, standing on a low round stone platform 4.0 m across and 0.3 m tall. An adult reads about 1.7 m against it: head level with the door's upper third, well below the brass collar. The silver ribbon is 0.15 m wide and rises straight up out of the frame; it never bends, never sways, and is never a tower or scaffold. State-dependent only. Camouflaged: living vines, broad leaves and leaf-shadow wrap the car and platform so it vanishes into the green. Master (found): the vines drawn aside, doors open, warm light inside. Ascending: the car alone on the ribbon high above the canopy, no platform in frame. Defunct: moss, cold shade, dulled brass, dark glass. Nothing is ever broken, shattered or ominous. Slightly taller than a garden shed at the base; a person boards it through a door they do not need to duck through. In the ascending state the car reads small against the sky, a bead on a silver thread. founder-heaven exactly as its reference plate: A floating protopian island in open sky above the jungle. Underneath, a gentle teardrop of pale rock trailing thin skirts of mist. On top, terraced gardens stepping up from the rim, low cream buildings with warm windows, slender brass wind-spires, small orchards and pools. It floats free: no chains, no pillars, no engines. Two fixed camera angles: ESTABLISHING (from below, over the jungle canopy) and TERRACE (standing on a rim garden terrace looking along the edge, jungle far below like a green sea). From below, the island sits high in the frame with canopy or clearing in the lower third; it is never close enough to read individual doors. On the terrace, the rim rail and the drop beyond it carry the height; buildings stay low and behind, sky stays generous. Pale terraced stone, green gardens, low cream buildings with warm windows, brass wind-spires, soft banners without lettering, drifting small clouds. Futuristic reads as graceful and quiet, never chrome, never neon, never engines or thrusters. The island reads about the size of a small hill town: whole gardens and rooftops are visible at once from below, and birds passing near it read as specks. From the terrace, the jungle below reads as a soft green sea with no individual trees. They are ordinary unnamed people with no identity beyond what the scene says, and they are not any named character. NOBODY ELSE APPEARS. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic. ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. DIRECTION OF TRAVEL. If a person in this scene is moving toward something, that destination MUST BE AHEAD OF THEM IN THE FRAME and they must be seen FROM BEHIND or from three-quarters behind, so the viewer is following them into it. A figure whose face is toward the camera is walking AWAY from everything behind them: if the thing they are moving toward is drawn behind them, the picture says the opposite of the scene. Their feet, hips, shoulders and gaze all point the same way, along the direction of travel. HANDS. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Two hands that come near each other stay SEPARATE and readable as two hands: they never merge into one mass, never share fingers and never fuse at the knuckles. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
